  - PRE-FLIGHT FINDING (rate-limit tier): `rateLimiters.public` is `limit=10/min` (not 30/min as .whatsnext said). Even stricter than expected — no change needed. The existing rate-limit call at top of placeOrderAsCustomer already covers the new xendit-path procedure invocation.
  - ATOMICITY DESIGN: Xendit call lives INSIDE the $transaction callback. Trade-off: external HTTP call holds row locks. Mitigated by (a) xendit-node SDK has timeouts, (b) any throw propagates → Prisma rolls back → no orphaned order. Alternative (call Xendit OUTSIDE transaction, write order after) would leave dangling Xendit invoices for orders that fail post-commit. Atomicity wins for payment surfaces.
  - HELPER ERROR HANDLING: helper wraps Xendit call in try/catch, re-throws as TRPCError(INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) with original error as `cause`. Both callers (admin protected procedure + public guest procedure) get consistent error type while preserving original message for debugging.
  - RED-PHASE GOTCHA: 2 of 5 new tests accidentally passed on first run — xendit-failure (Zod rejecting "xendit" enum throws the same way as expected Xendit-side rejection) and cod-regression (no change needed for cod path). Tightened xendit-failure to assert specific "unreachable-marker" error message + `expect(mockCreateInvoice).toHaveBeenCalled()` — forces a true RED because Zod's enum error doesn't contain the marker and procedure doesn't reach Xendit pre-implementation. Cod-regression left as-is: pre-passing is correct (no change to cod), post-passing proves xendit branch is gated correctly.
  - LINT GOTCHA: `as any` casts used during RED phase (when Zod enum didn't include "xendit") became dead code post-GREEN. ESLint `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion` flagged both occurrences. Used Edit replace_all to clean up. Lesson: always grep `as any` post-GREEN and remove dead casts.
